definitions.explanation: A person who uses magic. Commonly appears in fairy tales, fantasy stories, and games. Composed of 魔法 (magic) + 使い (user). Can refer to both male and female magic users.

examples.japanese: {魔法使|まほうつか}い⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{呪文|じゅもん}→呪文：11843_jumon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}えた→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{魔法使|まほうつか}いだ。
examples.english: The protagonist of this story is a young wizard.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、{魔法使|まほうつか}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なりたい→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}っていた→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, I wanted to become a wizard.

notes:
USAGE:
{魔法使|まほうつか}い is the most common and general word for a magic user in Japanese. It is gender-neutral and appears frequently in children's stories, fantasy literature, anime, and video games.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔法使|まほうつか}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{弟子|でし}→弟子：03986_deshi⟧ (wizard's apprentice)
- {魔法使|まほうつか}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{杖|つえ}→杖：12862_tsue⟧ (wizard's staff/wand)
- {魔法使|まほうつか}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become a wizard)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{魔女|まじょ}→魔女：14641_majo⟧ specifically means 'witch' (female), while {魔法使|まほうつか}い is gender-neutral. {魔術師|まじゅつし} sounds more formal and literary.
